clue.text: Would he shrink from carrying out his agreement?

definitions.text: Would he shrink from carrying out his agreement?

parts.words: Would he shrink from carrying out his agreement?
parts.note: two senses of one trade word: someone who shrinks (gets smaller) and someone who carries out an agreed contract of work; the question asks whether a builder would shirk his deal

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone would back out of a deal he has made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like 'back out', but it points to the other sense of the answer: something that contracts, or gets smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder or supplier who agrees to do work for a fixed price is one bound by a contract, and a muscle that shortens also contracts.

parts.note: a slap with the open hand, and also the end of a sleeve, which sits by the hand

explanation.surface: A question about a strike with the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a light slap; the other is the end of a shirt sleeve, located 'by the hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap given with the open palm, and the band at the end of a sleeve beside the wrist.

definitions.meaning: in the Book of Common Prayer catechism

explanation.surface: A clue about a particular kind of religious text.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prayer Book catechism asks 'What is your name?' and the printed answer is 'N. or M.', standing for the name to be supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard pattern is a type, and the catechism prints 'N or M' for the name.

clue.text: Yield once more and give sum up

parts.note: the prefix RE means again
to capitulate is to surrender, to give in

explanation.surface: An instruction to surrender again and then summarise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surrender word comes first in the clue but after RE in the answer; 'and give' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over the main points again briefly is to summarise them.

indicators.note: say marks that the word is spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast

explanation.surface: A remark about a category for performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' turns the cast of a play into the Hindu social rank of the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank in Hindu society, and by extension any social group.

parts.note: approaches or proposals, and also the opening pieces an orchestra plays

explanation.surface: A question about proposals made to sportsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests sportsmen being offered a deal, but they are musicians, who play the opening pieces of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Proposals or approaches are one sense, and orchestral introductions played before an opera are another.

clue.text: Music-maker is heard to make overture to a dandy

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase is heard, so the spoken sound of the next words gives the entry

parts.note: to make an overture to someone is to address them, 'O ...!', and a dandy is a beau, so the greeting is 'O beau'

explanation.surface: A musician seems to be chatting up a fashionable young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overture' looks musical in a clue about a music-maker, but here it means an approach or greeting: 'O beau!' said out loud gives the woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is a thing that makes music.

clue.text: Provides a passage for the intelligent emigrant?

definitions.text: Provides a passage for the intelligent emigrant?

parts.words: Provides a passage for the intelligent emigrant?
parts.note: the loss of clever, skilled people moving abroad, pictured as a channel that lets the clever thing in the head flow away

explanation.surface: A remark about arranging a sea voyage for a clever person leaving the country.
explanation.walkthrough: A drain is a passage for flow, and a brain is an intelligent person, so a drain for brains is the emigration of the skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the emigration of highly skilled or educated people to other countries.

clue.text: Woman appears to object about transport for all

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the woman and the object together surround the railway

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, is a crossword favourite for 'woman'
an object is a thing
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a means of transport

explanation.surface: A woman seems to protest about travel provision for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, 'protest', but it is a noun. 'Appears to' joins the woman to the object, and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole of something, each and every part, is all of it.

indicators.note: building here means putting together, so the letters of the following words are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone foresees that terraced houses will be put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' rearranges OF TERRACES. The definition is a phrase for a person, a weather or racing tipster.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather or racing tipster is a person who says what will happen next.

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit is one kind of legal action, as in a court hearing

explanation.surface: A remark about what state a set of clothes is in.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of things is one sense of the word, and a lawsuit heard in court is another.

definitions.meaning: ointments or coats of paint applied to a surface
formal written requests, as for a job

explanation.surface: A question about what goes on requests.
explanation.definitionFit: Ointments or coats applied to a surface are one sense, and formal requests are another.

clue.text: The face or the fortune sought by Ithaca wooers?

definitions.text: The face or the fortune sought by Ithaca wooers?

parts.words: The face or the fortune sought by Ithaca wooers?
parts.note: Penelope's suitors on Ithaca, in the Odyssey, chased either her lovely face (..., short for Penelope) or her wealth (a large sum)

explanation.surface: A question about whether Penelope's suitors were after her looks or her money.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey, while Odysseus is away, suitors besiege his wife Penelope on Ithaca. The phrase reads both as 'a lovely Penelope' and as the idiom for a great deal of money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a large sum of money, and read literally it also describes a beautiful Penelope.

parts.note: people who play golf together on a links course, and in general colleagues joined in business

explanation.surface: A question about golfing companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Links' reads as a golf course but also as a verb, 'connects', and the word means partners or colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleagues or partners joined with one another in an enterprise.

parts.note: Omar Khayyam was a poet from Persia, and a mouser is a household pet that catches mice

explanation.surface: A question about the poet Omar's device for catching rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: Omar Khayyam, of the Rubaiyat, came from Persia; the long-haired breed of feline named after that country is his 'mouse-trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-haired breed of domestic feline from Persia, and felines catch mice.

clue.text: He looks on port, etc, as out of place

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are not in their proper positions, so these words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a list of wines and the like, all in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of place' rearranges the letters of PORT, ETC and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone watching a match or show without taking part is an onlooker.

clue.text: Might be taken in hand at board meeting

definitions.text: Might be taken in hand at board meeting

parts.words: Might be taken in hand at board meeting
parts.note: the board is a dining table, and the meeting is a meal, where cutlery and plates are held

explanation.surface: Business that might be dealt with at a company directors' meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests directors, but it is the old word for a dining table; what you hold at a meal is the knives, forks and plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cutlery and dishes used for serving and eating food.

clue.text: A staggering situation for those who are left? '

definitions.text: A staggering situation for those who are left?

parts.words: A staggering situation for those who are left?
parts.note: a word for a stagger or sudden sway, which also completes the idiom 'left in the ...', meaning abandoned in difficulty

explanation.surface: A remark about how shocking it is for people who have been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' looks like 'shocking', but it means swaying: a sudden sway is one sense, and those deserted are 'left in the' same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden unsteady sway is one meaning, and to be abandoned in trouble is to be 'left in' one.

indicators.note: the numeral comes to conclude, meaning it is placed at the very end

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, flowing through York
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword standby for 'many'

explanation.surface: A bird is seen at the river, as many people agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclude' looks like 'decide', but it puts L at the end. The OUSE is an English river, through York.
explanation.definitionFit: An old spelling of the ouzel, the blackbird or water songbird.

clue.text: Division of the Purchase Department, say

indicators.note: say marks that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: purchase means buy and a department is a section, so this is a 'buy section'

explanation.surface: A clue about a part of the office that does the buying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' turns 'buy section' into a word for cutting something into two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting into two equal halves is a kind of splitting apart.

parts.note: in hunting, those present when the fox is killed are there at the end of the chase; 'killing time' is the idiom for passing the hours idly

explanation.surface: A question about a gift meant to help pass the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as 'gift', but it means 'there'; 'killing time' is not idling but the moment of the kill in a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means being there at the finish, first of a hunt's kill and then of any climax.

parts.note: east is one quarter of the compass
south is a second compass quarter
south-east is a third compass direction
north is the fourth compass quarter

explanation.surface: A remark about four districts somewhere in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass gives the four pieces E, S, SE and N; the definition is the place, a city in the Ruhr.
explanation.definitionFit: A large industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

indicators.note: the plural 'degrees' builds the word from more than one of the same degree, so the abbreviation is used twice over

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A barrier on a river is constructed in stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' reads as a river barrier but is an animal's mother; 'by degrees' looks like 'gradually' but builds the word from two Master of Arts degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is an animal's mother, and the child's word for mother has the same meaning.

definitions.meaning: fierce or ruthless, as in 'one ... swoop'
the rhyme 'I do not love thee

explanation.surface: A description of a heartless, unpopular physician.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme, by Tom Brown, runs 'I do not love thee, Doctor Fell, the reason why I cannot tell'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word meaning fierce or ruthless, and the doctor in the rhyme whom the speaker did not love.

definitions.meaning: the check mark a teacher puts against a right answer

explanation.surface: A question about a second sign of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief moment and a check mark showing something is right are both senses.

indicators.note: types here suggests the letters can be set out in different forms, so the poets and Asian are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of ardent writers from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Types' rearranges POETS and ASIAN; the dash is punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervid means burning with strong feeling, ardent.

definitions.meaning: collections or groups of things, as in a chess set
in tennis a match is made of these, each a group of games

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how many games there are.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of matching items is one sense, and in tennis a group of games is another.

clue.text: Item in the Dauphin's gift to Henry V'

definitions.text: Item in the Dauphin's gift to Henry V

parts.words: Item in the Dauphin's gift to Henry V
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Henry V the French prince sends a mocking barrel of sporting balls, hinting the king is fit only for games

explanation.surface: A reference to the insulting present in Shakespeare's history play.
explanation.walkthrough: In Act 1 of Henry V the Dauphin mocks young Henry with a tun of these balls, and Henry replies with war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dauphin's insulting gift was a barrel of sporting balls used on a court.
